Inside that minute the only entity showing its own failure evidence is the frontend-proxy workload. At 2026-11-23T22:45:04Z the frontend-proxy Deployment (the only Deployment in the namespace at generation 2, updated by manager "OpenAPI-Generator" rather than helm) rolled out new ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-7b7cd5fb4 replacing frontend-proxy-579d54f6f5, and the resulting pod's container spec lists FRONTEND_HOST twice, first "frontend" and last "localhost", so the value substituted into Envoy's envsubst template is localhost. The pre-change pod held a flat ~19 MB working set against a 65Mi limit; the new pod was only at ~2.2 MB when the window closed, so the memory growth and the causal link from FRONTEND_HOST=localhost to the OOM are inferred rather than observed, which is why this assessment is partial. The 500/503 client-side errors seen at 22:44:36-22:45:00Z predate the change and coincide with services still starting after the fresh rollout, so they are treated as start-up transients, not as this fault.

No networkpolicies and no resourcequotas exist in astronomy-shop, and every service endpoint listed (including frontend-proxy 10.244.125.9 and checkout 10.244.125.13) has a ready address, so the observed refused connections are not explained by network policy, quota or missing endpoints.

Error log lines in the window are concentrated at start-up: the frontend logged 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.34.16:8080' at 22:44:43Z (10.96.34.16:8080 is the checkout Service clusterIP), and many services reported OTLP export failures to otel-collector ports 4317/4318 between 22:44:41Z and 22:45:14Z; the checkout container itself only started at 22:44:38Z.

The load generator recorded locust_errors for GET "/" (503), GET /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, GET /api/product-reviews/0PUK6V6EV0, GET /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM and GET /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z (500), with an aggregated fail_ratio of 0.125 in the 22:45:00Z fetch report.

Those 500/503 client errors are not evidence of the frontend-proxy change: they were observed at 22:44:36-22:45:00Z, before the Deployment update at 22:45:04Z, and they coincide with the fresh rollout (checkout started 22:44:38Z, product-catalog 22:44:29Z, otel-collector still restarting), so they are attributed to start-up transients rather than to the injected setting.

Span data available up to the rollout shows healthy edge traffic: frontend-proxy spans between 22:44:55Z and 22:45:02Z carry http.status_code 200 (and one 308), with zero error-tagged rows in that sampled view.
The Kafka path is healthy at query time: topics are __consumer_offsets and orders, consumer groups accounting and fraud-detection are STABLE with lag 0 on orders partition 0.

Prometheus exposes trace-derived series names traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket/count/sum, and the status_code label values present on traces_span_metrics_calls_total are STATUS_CODE_OK and STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no STATUS_CODE_ERROR value is listed).

Mechanism (inferred, not directly observed): because FRONTEND_HOST resolves to localhost, the Envoy frontend cluster rendered into the new frontend-proxy pod points at 127.0.0.1:8080, its own listener, so requests destined for the frontend loop back into the same process until the 65Mi limit is exhausted, producing the observed OOMKilled exit 137 and CrashLoopBackOff and leaving the edge without a working proxy; the rendered envoy.yaml and post-22:45:16 logs needed to prove the loop were not observable.

Alternative candidate still open: the OOM could come from a cause other than the FRONTEND_HOST override (for example a heavier baseline request load on the newly started pod), since no in-window sample shows the new pod's memory actually crossing 65Mi; counter-evidence is that the pre-change pod stayed flat near 19MB and no other pod in the namespace restarted.

Advisory: compare the frontend-proxy Deployment against the helm release values to confirm the duplicate FRONTEND_HOST entry (value localhost) was added out of band, remove that override so FRONTEND_HOST is frontend, then verify the replacement pod stays well under its 65Mi limit and that GET / returns 200 through the proxy.

Watch frontend-proxy restart count, container_memory_working_set_bytes versus the 65Mi limit and Envoy 503/504 rates over the next few minutes to confirm or refute the self-referential-routing hypothesis.
